complexity_ledger.narrative: MF-038 measured the one number the modular-fuzzing value proposition rests on: do the generated cases catch real bugs? Control on the reduced runnable corpus (14 representative cases spanning every runnable filesystem command) was GREEN, so the measurement is meaningful (MF-016's own safeguard). Kill rate = 4/13 = 0.308. The four killed mutants are all STRUCTURAL bugs that change which directory or lifecycle tree gets created (wrong program_model dir, wrong desired_program_model dir, wrong tickets/<id> dir, ticket desired-tree never created); three were caught via before-state replay divergence and one (open ticket wrong dir) via a clean projected ticket_state conformance mismatch. All NINE subtle bugs SURVIVED: empty Internal.tla, wrong manifest enums (model_role, workflow), three neighbouring/off-by-one budget defaults, a wrong manifest field value, a wrong ticket_plan phase enum, and a misplaced results/.gitkeep. Root cause is uniform: the adapters project a real repository into 9 model variables that are functions of directory/file EXISTENCE and exit codes only -- no oracle reads file content, a budget value, a manifest field, an enum, or a count. The cases are existence-and-exit-code oracles, not content oracles. Full analysis and the per-survivor refine_variable/refine_action pointers: results/kill-rate-report.md and results/kill-rate-report.json. Recommendation to the owner: NOT yet ship-worthy as "case advising" on bug-catching strength (0.308, and lower under a realistically subtle catalog); the highest-value deepening is to project the CONTENT the commands produce (budget block, manifest status/model_role, ticket_plan phase) into model variables so those survivors become killable. The number was not tuned in any direction: 9 of 13 mutants are subtle and all 9 survived; no threshold lowered, no survivor deleted, ignored_suppression_keys none. Validation matrix green: TLC 231,621 distinct / depth 25 (zero delta), spec-unit 63+60 passed, repo units 526 passed (>=522 baseline), specWorkflow 8/8, cliWorkflow 2/2.

ticket.objective: INVESTIGATION TICKET, deliverable is a measured kill rate not a feature. Answers the one question the fuzzing value-proposition rests on and never answered against a runnable corpus: DO THE GENERATED CASES CATCH REAL BUGS? The kill test (MF-016) is the only instrument that measures bug-catching power and has never produced a real number here -- its worked example was synthetic (4/7 on a toy), and against the real corpus it control_failed because no case ran. MF-031/MF-032 made ~10% of the corpus (the filesystem-mutating commands) executable, so the experiment is finally possible. Establish a GREEN CONTROL first (unmutated runnable corpus must pass, or the rate is meaningless -- report and stop). Seed >=10 realistic bugs across the runnable adapters (ScaffoldProject, ScaffoldWorkflow, RecordBudgets, OpenTicket, InstallLocalCli, UpdateTicketDesired/Current), spanning obvious (wrong file, wrong output) and SUBTLE (off-by-one count, plausible-but-wrong phase, neighbouring budget default, dropped field) -- the subtle ones are the real test and trivial-only seeding inflates the rate. Run cases against each mutant; a mutant is killed if some oracle (output/projected-state/effect conformance) catches the divergence. Report the kill rate, per-bug kill/survive, and for each survivor WHY the cases missed it. HONEST-OUTCOME RULE: a low kill rate is a valid valuable result -- do not tune it, do not seed only catchable bugs, do not delete a survivor; MF-016 nearly shipped a spurious perfect rate and caught itself. Recommend whether model-derived conformance testing is worth shipping as case-advising based on the number. See tickets/038-kill-rate-probe.md.
